Hi Rachel,

Thanks for sending the completed SIG sections last week. GreenFintech is consolidating vendor incident response requirements ahead of an upcoming audit — I have two quick clarifications:

1) Can you map Redwood's breach-notice timelines to region (US/EU/APAC)? Specifically: regulator notification windows (where applicable), customer notification targets, and internal detection-to-notification SLAs.

2) We also need a single point of contact for each region for incident intake (security team or on-call) and an escalation roster for executive notices.

Please attach any evidence (SOC 2 snapshot, IR policy excerpt, contact matrix) you can share under NDA. Procurement is copied for reference.

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: incident notification timelines and regional contacts

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front, details below and I'll attach a matrix and SOC 2 snapshot after we confirm NDA scope:

- Regulator windows: US (state-level breach laws vary; we aim for "as soon as reasonably practicable" and notify customers within 72 hours if PII loss is confirmed), EU (where GDPR applies, we notify Supervisory Authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach that triggers reporting), APAC (varies by country; we follow local law and notify customers within 5 business days by default unless shorter windows apply).

- Customer notification: our target is preliminary customer notice within 72 hours of confirmed impact; full incident report within 30 days.

- Internal/exec escalation: see roster below — primary security on-call, secondary CS lead, exec on-call for SLA exceptions.

I'll circulate the attachment with an IR contact matrix and redacted policy excerpts once procurement confirms the NDA addendum (we usually include SIG evidence under our standard DPA + evidence addendum).

--
Rachel Kim
Head of Security & Trust (acting)
Redwood Inference

Elena — good questions. Short answers and attached artifacts (see attachment list).

- "Becoming aware": For GDPR reporting we interpret "becoming aware" as the point where we have a reasonable belief that a personal data breach has occurred and a controller-level assessment indicates the breach is likely to result in a risk to data subjects. In practice we treat high-confidence detections as triggers for the 72-hour clock; lower-confidence events start an accelerated investigation but we do not automatically file a supervisory authority notification until we have a controller assessment. We documented this in the IR policy excerpt.

- Templates: attached are a redacted customer notification template (customer-notice-template.txt) and an executive escalation template (exec-escalation-example.txt). We redact customer-identifying details and legal language.

- Evidence delivery: happy to drop the XLSX and SOC2 redaction into your shared Drive folder (link above) or send via DocuSign if procurement prefers. For now I've uploaded the IR matrix and SOC 2 snapshot to our secure evidence folder and shared a view-only link.

Attachments included: redwood-sig-IR-matrix.xlsx, redwood-soc2-snapshot.pdf, customer-notice-template.txt, exec-escalation-example.txt

If you need us to pre-populate the notification with a sample timeline keyed to your account (impact window, tokens affected, first detection time), we can do that — we will need GreenFintech's internal contact for the sample (name + email) to demonstrate the flow in the template.

Thanks,
Rachel
Head of Security & Trust (acting)
Redwood Inference
